question: Which proof systems and circuit languages can I use for a zero-knowledge application on Stellar, and how are proofs verified on-chain?

golden.answer: Stellar does not mandate Noir or any single ZK toolchain. Builders can use Circom/Groth16, Noir-based systems, or zkVM workflows such as RISC Zero, provided they supply a compatible Soroban verifier. On-chain verification uses a verifier contract plus native cryptographic host functions where applicable; Protocol 25 made BN254 and Poseidon/Poseidon2 primitives available, but those primitives do not by themselves create an end-to-end privacy system.
keyFacts: States that Stellar does not require Noir.
Covers multiple proof systems and circuit languages that target Soroban verifiers.
Proofs use compatible Soroban verifier logic/native host functions per curve/primitives.
Lists Protocol 25 BN254 and Poseidon/Poseidon2 building blocks.
Protocol 25 does not provide an automatic private-payment system.
avoid: Noir is the only supported way to build ZK applications on Stellar.
Protocol 25 automatically makes every Stellar payment private.
golden.notes: Status-sensitive details are stated as of 2026-07-11; grade later sourced changes leniently and require dated primary evidence. As of 2026-11-02, the Stellar privacy docs and the rs-soroban-ultrahonk verifier README say that verifier accepts only non-zero-knowledge UltraHonk proofs (no witness hiding); do not penalize an answer that states this limit.
